industry_workflow.overview: HOW PROFESSIONAL SOFTWARE GETS BUILT: The complete 13-step software engineering lifecycle taught throughout the Nova Skills curriculum:

stages.name: Requirement & User Stories
stages.desc: Deconstruct business requirements into user stories, acceptance criteria, and edge-case definitions.

stages.name: UI / Wireframe & Component Hierarchy
stages.desc: Map user interfaces into modular component trees, identifying state boundaries and props flow.

stages.name: Frontend UI Implementation
stages.desc: Build responsive, accessible, mobile-first user interfaces using TypeScript, React/Next.js, and Tailwind.

stages.name: API Contract & Schema Design
stages.desc: Define RESTful endpoint specifications, request payloads, response schemas, and error structures.

stages.name: Backend Business Logic
stages.desc: Implement robust server logic using layered Node.js/Express controllers, services, and validation.

stages.name: Database Schema & Migrations
stages.desc: Design normalized PostgreSQL tables, foreign key constraints, indexes, and versioned Prisma migrations.

stages.name: Authentication & Authorization (RBAC)
stages.desc: Secure endpoints with bcrypt password hashing, JWTs, HTTP-only cookies, and role-based permissions.

stages.name: Automated Testing Suite
stages.desc: Execute automated unit tests (Vitest), integration tests, and Playwright end-to-end verification.

stages.name: Peer Code Review & Linting
stages.desc: Audit pull requests against style guides, security standards, maintainability, and naming clarity.

stages.name: Git Feature Branch & Pull Request
stages.desc: Commit clean, atomic code changes and open pull requests with detailed descriptions and issue links.

stages.name: CI/CD Build & Container Deployment
stages.desc: Trigger automated GitHub Actions pipelines to run tests, build Docker containers, and deploy to staging.

stages.name: Production Monitoring & Error Logging
stages.desc: Verify live deployment health through application logs, error tracking, and uptime monitors.

stages.name: Performance Tuning & Improvement
stages.desc: Profile database queries, cache frequent endpoints, audit Core Web Vitals, and refactor bottlenecks.

faq.question: Is this course suitable for complete beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. The program is designed from first principles. Module 1 starts with how the internet and client-server architectures work, followed by semantic HTML and CSS, before advancing into JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Node.js, databases, and deployment. No prior programming background is required, but you must be prepared to write code and debug regularly.

faq.question: Do I need prior coding experience before joining?
faq.answer: No prior coding experience is necessary. What you need is basic computer literacy, problem-solving curiosity, text typing ability, and the discipline to complete weekly coding labs. We teach you how to think like an engineer from day one.

faq.question: Will HTML and CSS be taught from basics?
faq.answer: Yes, absolutely. Modules 2 and 3 teach semantic HTML5, accessible form validation, document outlines, CSS cascade, specificity, the box model, Flexbox, CSS Grid, mobile-first responsive design, and Tailwind CSS. We ensure you build rock-solid layout fundamentals before moving to frontend frameworks.

faq.question: Is JavaScript thoroughly included?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 4 is dedicated entirely to modern JavaScript (ES6+). You will master variables, data types, arrow functions, scope, closures, higher-order array methods (map, filter, reduce), DOM manipulation, event delegation, promises, async/await, and fetching data from REST APIs.

faq.question: Is TypeScript included in the curriculum?
faq.answer: Yes. TypeScript is a mandatory core module (Module 5) and is used throughout the rest of the course across both React and Node.js. You will learn interfaces, type aliases, union types, type narrowing, generics, component prop typing, and type-safe API contracts.

faq.question: Will I learn React?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 6 provides deep training in React 19 application engineering. You will learn component decomposition, JSX/TSX, state management with useState and useReducer, lifecycle side-effects with useEffect, custom hooks, the Context API, and building modular, testable user interfaces.

faq.question: Will Next.js be taught?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 7 covers Next.js with the modern App Router. You will learn nested layouts, dynamic routes, React Server Components vs Client Components, server actions, data fetching patterns, image optimization, SEO metadata, and production deployment workflows.

faq.question: Is Node.js included in the program?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 8 covers backend engineering with Node.js and Express. You will learn event-driven runtime architecture, modular routing, custom middleware, the controller-service-repository pattern, request validation, environment configuration, and structured error handling.

faq.question: Which database will I learn?
faq.answer: You will learn PostgreSQL, the industry's most respected open-source relational database. We also cover modern Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) using Prisma to manage schemas, migrations, and type-safe database queries.

faq.question: Will PostgreSQL and relational SQL be covered deeply?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 10 is dedicated to SQL and PostgreSQL. You will learn relational database design, table normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF), primary and foreign keys, complex JOINs, aggregations, GROUP BY, transactions (ACID), indexes, and performance query tuning before introducing the Prisma ORM.

faq.question: Will I learn how to build REST APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 9 focuses on REST API engineering. You will learn HTTP methods, status codes, query/path parameters, JSON serialization, payload validation, pagination, filtering, search, versioning, Postman testing, and designing predictable API contracts.

faq.question: Will authentication and authorization be included?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 11 is dedicated to authentication and authorization. You will implement secure user registration, bcrypt password hashing, session tokens, JWTs with HTTP-only cookie storage, token refresh rotation, and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) across frontend and backend routes.

faq.question: Will application security be taught?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 12 covers defensive web application security based on the OWASP Top 10. You will learn to prevent SQL injection, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), CSRF attacks, CORS misconfigurations, broken access control, insecure secrets management (.env), and rate limiting.

faq.question: Will I learn software testing?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 13 makes testing mandatory. You will learn unit testing for business logic, component testing for React UI using Vitest and React Testing Library, API integration testing, and end-to-end browser user flows using Playwright.

faq.question: Is Git and GitHub included throughout the course?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 14 teaches Git and GitHub, but Git is used continuously from your very first project. You will master git init, branching, committing, pull requests, resolving merge conflicts, writing meaningful commit messages, and managing project boards on GitHub.

faq.question: Will I work with Pull Requests and code reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. In Module 14, Module 16, and during the Team Software Engineering Sprint, all project features must be submitted via GitHub Pull Requests. You will participate in weekly code review labs where trainers and peers review your code against professional maintainability standards.

faq.question: Will I learn Docker?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 18 introduces Docker containerization for developers. You will learn container concepts, write multi-stage Dockerfiles, build and run container images, configure port mappings, and use Docker Compose to run your web application and PostgreSQL database locally with consistency.

faq.question: Will deployment be taught?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 19 covers production deployment across modern cloud platforms. You will deploy frontend applications to Vercel and backend services and databases to Render or cloud providers, configuring custom domains, HTTPS, and production environment variables.

faq.question: Will CI/CD fundamentals be covered?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 19 introduces Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) using GitHub Actions. You will build automated workflows that run linting, execute automated tests on every pull request, and deploy code automatically upon merging.

faq.question: Will Python be taught in this course?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 17 covers supporting Python for developers. You will learn Python fundamentals, file handling, data structures, making HTTP requests, writing developer automation scripts, and integrating external AI/LLM web services.

faq.question: Is Python the main backend technology in this course?
faq.answer: No. The primary production full-stack path is JavaScript/TypeScript with Node.js, Express, and PostgreSQL. Python is taught as a valuable supporting skill for automation, scripting, and AI integration, keeping the main 6-month production stack focused and coherent.

faq.question: Will modern AI coding tools be taught?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 16 teaches modern AI-assisted software development using tools like Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and Claude. You will learn prompt patterns for code explanation, boilerplate generation, refactoring, test scaffolding, and documentation.

faq.question: Will AI build the projects for me?
faq.answer: No. AI is taught strictly as an engineering assistant. In Nova Skills, every student must understand, explain, debug, and defend every line of code they commit. You must complete oral viva examinations and project defense sessions where AI cannot assist you.

faq.question: How many practical projects will I build?
faq.answer: You will build 6 practical engineering projects (Responsive Business Site, React Productivity App, Auth & RBAC System, Full-Stack Booking App, SaaS Dashboard, Team Project) plus 1 comprehensive production SaaS capstone.

faq.question: Will I work on team engineering projects?
faq.answer: Yes. In the signature Software Engineering Sprint (Module 14 & Project 6), you will collaborate in squads of 3–4 learners using GitHub Issues, feature branches, pull requests, sprint boards, and peer code reviews to experience real workplace engineering dynamics.

faq.question: Will I create a professional GitHub portfolio?
faq.answer: Yes. You will build a recruiter-ready GitHub profile with pinned repositories, clean commit histories, detailed architecture diagrams, live deployment links, test badges, and comprehensive README documentation for all major projects.

faq.question: Is technical interview preparation included?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 22 covers practical Data Structures & Algorithms (30–40 targeted interview problems), and Module 23 covers technical interview preparation: JavaScript/React/SQL/API viva practice, system design diagrams, resume polish, and oral project defense.

faq.question: What realistic job roles does this course prepare me for?
faq.answer: This course prepares you for realistic entry and junior software engineering roles: Junior Full-Stack Developer, Junior Frontend Developer, Junior React Developer, Junior Backend Developer, Junior Web Developer, Software Developer Intern, or Freelance Web Developer. We focus on building verifiable competence rather than making false claims of senior-level placement.

lessons.what_is_taught: Parameterized queries vs string concatenation; Object-Level Authorization verifying resource ownership (req.user.id).

lessons.what_learner_does: Refactors raw concatenated SQL queries into parameterized queries and adds user ownership checks.
lessons.expected_outcome: Endpoints immune to SQL injection and unauthorized record access.

lessons.what_learner_does: Implements input sanitization and configures Content Security Policy headers blocking inline script execution.
lessons.expected_outcome: Frontend and backend protected against script injection attacks.

lessons.lesson_title: API Hardening: CORS, Rate Limiting & Secrets Management

lessons.what_learner_does: Configures Helmet headers, strict CORS origin policies, and IP rate limiters on login endpoints.
lessons.expected_outcome: Hardened API gateway with rate limiting and secure headers.

modules.hands_on_practice: Write Python scripts to automate local developer tasks, parse JSON files, and consume external web APIs.
modules.assignment: Create a Python developer automation script that fetches data from an API, processes records, and generates a formatted report.
modules.business_application: Python is the undisputed language of automation, data engineering, and modern AI/LLM tool integrations.
modules.expected_outcome: Working Python automation scripts capable of handling files, API requests, and data transformations.

modules.module_purpose: Understand containerization fundamentals, writing Dockerfiles, and orchestrating local multi-container environments.
what_you_will_learn: Master the core principles of Docker & Development Environments.
Implement production-grade practical code following modern industry best practices.
Systematically troubleshoot, test, and debug common real-world errors in this domain.

lessons.lesson_title: Why Containers: What Docker Solves for Developers
lessons.what_is_taught: Virtual machines vs containers, dependency isolation, environment parity, and the Docker engine architecture.
lessons.why_it_matters: Ensures every engineer on a team and every production server runs the exact same software environment.
lessons.what_learner_does: Installs Docker, runs basic test containers, and inspects running container processes via Docker CLI.
lessons.expected_outcome: Clear conceptual model of containerization and container lifecycles.

lessons.lesson_title: Writing Dockerfiles & Building Container Images
lessons.what_is_taught: FROM, WORKDIR, COPY, RUN, EXPOSE, CMD/ENTRYPOINT instructions, .dockerignore, and image layer caching.
lessons.why_it_matters: Enables packaging full-stack code and dependencies into portable, immutable executable images.
lessons.what_learner_does: Writes a Dockerfile for an Express.js backend, builds the image, and verifies local container execution.
lessons.expected_outcome: Working container image running an Express web service.

lessons.lesson_title: Port Mapping, Environment Variables & Volume Concepts
lessons.what_is_taught: -p port forwarding, passing -e environment variables at runtime, and volume mounting for live development.
lessons.why_it_matters: Allows accessing containerized web apps from the host browser while keeping sensitive secrets configurable.
lessons.what_learner_does: Runs a containerized API with port mapping and injects database credentials via environment variables.
lessons.expected_outcome: Accessible containerized application with dynamic environment configuration.

lessons.lesson_title: Local Multi-Container Stacks with Docker Compose
lessons.what_is_taught: docker-compose.yml syntax, defining web and db services, container networks, and volume persistence for PostgreSQL.
lessons.why_it_matters: Spins up an entire full-stack system (app + database) with a single command without installing local databases.
lessons.what_learner_does: Writes a docker-compose.yml orchestrating a Node.js API and PostgreSQL container with persistent volume data.
lessons.expected_outcome: One-command local full-stack development environment via Docker Compose.

modules.hands_on_practice: Dockerize a full-stack application and run Node.js and PostgreSQL together using Docker Compose.
modules.assignment: Write a multi-stage Dockerfile for a Node.js API and a docker-compose.yml file linking it to PostgreSQL.
modules.business_application: Eliminates the dreaded 'it works on my machine' bug, ensuring 100% parity between local development and cloud production.
modules.expected_outcome: Containerized full-stack application running reliably inside Docker containers.

modules.module_purpose: Build automated Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment pipelines deploying to modern cloud infrastructure.
what_you_will_learn: Master the core principles of CI/CD & Deployment Fundamentals.
Implement production-grade practical code following modern industry best practices.
Systematically troubleshoot, test, and debug common real-world errors in this domain.

lessons.lesson_title: The Deployment Lifecycle: Build, Test & Release
lessons.what_is_taught: Development vs production builds, minification, tree-shaking, environment variable security, and cloud hosting tiers.
lessons.why_it_matters: Prepares raw source code into high-performance, secure production bundles ready for public traffic.
lessons.what_learner_does: Generates a production build of a Next.js application, inspecting bundle analysis and static output.
lessons.expected_outcome: Optimized production build ready for cloud deployment.

lessons.lesson_title: Continuous Integration with GitHub Actions
lessons.what_is_taught: CI concepts, .github/workflows YAML syntax, triggers (on: push, pull_request), jobs, steps, and action runners.
lessons.why_it_matters: Automatically prevents broken or untested code from ever being merged into main branches.
lessons.what_learner_does: Writes a GitHub Actions workflow that automatically installs dependencies, runs linters, and executes tests on PRs.
lessons.expected_outcome: Active GitHub Actions CI pipeline guarding repository merges.

lessons.lesson_title: Deploying Full-Stack Applications to the Cloud
lessons.what_is_taught: Deploying Next.js to Vercel, deploying Node.js web services to Render, and provisioning managed PostgreSQL instances.
lessons.why_it_matters: Provides live public URLs for your applications that recruiters and real users can interact with.
lessons.what_learner_does: Deploys a full-stack application connecting a Vercel frontend to a Render backend and managed PostgreSQL database.
lessons.expected_outcome: Live, public full-stack web application running on cloud infrastructure.

lessons.lesson_title: Custom Domains, SSL Certificates & Environment Isolation
lessons.what_is_taught: DNS records (A, CNAME), automated SSL/HTTPS encryption, and separating Staging vs Production environments.
lessons.why_it_matters: Gives applications professional branded domains while ensuring test data never pollutes production databases.
lessons.what_learner_does: Configures DNS settings, verifies SSL certificate issuance, and manages separate staging/production .env keys.
lessons.expected_outcome: Secure, custom-domain web application with production environment separation.

modules.hands_on_practice: Configure a GitHub Actions workflow that automatically runs linter and test suites on pull requests.
modules.assignment: Deploy a full-stack application with automated GitHub Actions CI/CD to Vercel (frontend) and Render (backend).
modules.business_application: Allows software teams to deploy features and bug fixes dozens of times per week with zero manual deployment errors.
modules.expected_outcome: Fully automated CI/CD pipeline verifying code quality and deploying to live cloud servers on git push.

modules.module_purpose: Learn how to monitor, diagnose, and optimize live production applications using logging, metrics, and error tracking.
what_you_will_learn: Master the core principles of Production Monitoring, Logging & Performance.
Implement production-grade practical code following modern industry best practices.
Systematically troubleshoot, test, and debug common real-world errors in this domain.

lessons.lesson_title: Structured Logging & Application Monitoring
lessons.what_is_taught: Log levels (info, warn, error), structured JSON logs with Winston, request correlation IDs, and log aggregation.
lessons.why_it_matters: Standard console.log statements are lost in production; structured logs enable searching and diagnosing live crashes.
lessons.what_learner_does: Replaces console.log with Winston structured logger recording timestamped JSON log events.
lessons.expected_outcome: Enterprise logging system generating searchable log entries.

lessons.lesson_title: API Health Checks & Uptime Monitoring
lessons.what_is_taught: Designing /health and /ready endpoints, database ping checks, and setting up automated external uptime monitors.
lessons.why_it_matters: Alerts the engineering team immediately when a server or database goes down before customers complain.
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a /health endpoint verifying PostgreSQL connectivity and configures an external uptime ping monitor.
lessons.expected_outcome: Automated uptime monitoring with live health check endpoint.

lessons.lesson_title: Frontend Performance & Core Web Vitals Optimization
lessons.what_is_taught: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), Interaction to Next Paint (INP), and asset compression.
lessons.why_it_matters: Google heavily penalizes slow websites in search rankings; fast loading directly increases user conversion rates.
lessons.what_learner_does: Audits a Next.js application, optimizes heavy images, eliminates layout shift, and boosts Lighthouse scores to 90+.
lessons.expected_outcome: High-performance frontend achieving green Core Web Vitals.

lessons.lesson_title: Database Query Optimization & Basic Caching
lessons.what_is_taught: Identifying slow queries, EXPLAIN ANALYZE in PostgreSQL, adding B-tree indexes, and in-memory caching concepts.
lessons.why_it_matters: Slow database queries are the primary bottleneck causing sluggish response times as user traffic scales.
lessons.what_learner_does: Uses EXPLAIN ANALYZE to identify an unindexed sequential scan and adds indexes to reduce query execution time by 90%.
lessons.expected_outcome: Optimized database queries with verified index performance gains.

modules.hands_on_practice: Implement structured JSON logging, health check endpoints, and profile slow database queries.
modules.assignment: Add production health monitoring, structured logging, and Core Web Vitals optimization to an existing application.
modules.business_application: Answers the critical engineering question: 'How do we know the deployed application is functioning properly right now?'
modules.expected_outcome: Production-ready application with automated error monitoring, health check endpoints, and high Core Web Vitals.

modules.module_purpose: Understand pragmatic, beginner-friendly system design principles, architectural patterns, and creating technical diagrams.
what_you_will_learn: Master the core principles of Practical System Design & Architecture.
Implement production-grade practical code following modern industry best practices.
Systematically troubleshoot, test, and debug common real-world errors in this domain.

lessons.lesson_title: System Design Foundations: Scaling Concepts & Trade-Offs
lessons.what_is_taught: Vertical vs horizontal scaling, load balancers, stateless servers, stateful databases, and latency vs throughput.
lessons.why_it_matters: Teaches engineers how systems grow from 100 users to 100,000 users without crashing.
lessons.what_learner_does: Analyzes system scaling bottlenecks and designs a horizontally scalable server architecture on paper.
lessons.expected_outcome: Clear conceptual grasp of scalability trade-offs and bottlenecks.

lessons.lesson_title: Architectural Patterns: Monoliths vs Modular Services
lessons.what_is_taught: Pros and cons of modular monoliths vs microservices; why startups should almost always build modular monoliths first.
lessons.why_it_matters: Prevents engineers from prematurely over-engineering complex microservices that cripple startup velocity.
lessons.what_learner_does: Evaluates architectural trade-offs for a new startup, justifying a modular monolith architecture.
lessons.expected_outcome: Written architectural justification report defending design decisions.

lessons.lesson_title: Storage, Caching & Content Delivery Networks (CDNs)
lessons.what_is_taught: Object storage (S3 concepts) for user media uploads, CDN edge caching for static assets, and Redis caching concepts.
lessons.why_it_matters: Keeps application servers fast and light by offloading heavy media files and static assets to specialized infrastructure.
lessons.what_learner_does: Diagrams the upload lifecycle of user images: direct upload to cloud storage with CDN distribution.
lessons.expected_outcome: Optimized media storage and caching architecture design.

lessons.lesson_title: Creating Technical System Architecture Diagrams
lessons.what_is_taught: Standard architectural diagramming symbols, component boundaries, data flow arrows, and sequence diagrams with Mermaid.
lessons.why_it_matters: Technical diagrams are the universal language used in senior technical interviews and corporate engineering design reviews.
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates a professional architectural diagram illustrating browser, Next.js frontend, Node API, PostgreSQL, and auth flow.
lessons.expected_outcome: Comprehensive, publication-quality system architecture diagram.

modules.hands_on_practice: Design and diagram the complete architecture for a scalable service booking or e-commerce platform.
modules.assignment: Create a comprehensive System Architecture Blueprint for your Capstone project including data flow and storage.
modules.business_application: Prepares engineers to make sound architectural trade-offs and communicate technical visions clearly to stakeholders.
modules.expected_outcome: Professional architectural diagram and written technical design specification for a web system.

modules.module_title: Data Structures, Algorithms & Coding Interview Prep
modules.module_purpose: Master practical data structures, algorithmic intuition, and solve 30–40 targeted coding interview challenges.
what_you_will_learn: Master the core principles of Data Structures, Algorithms & Coding Interview Prep.
Implement production-grade practical code following modern industry best practices.
Systematically troubleshoot, test, and debug common real-world errors in this domain.

lessons.lesson_title: Big-O Notation & Algorithmic Complexity Intuition
lessons.what_is_taught: Time and space complexity: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n^2); recognizing performance bottlenecks in code.
lessons.why_it_matters: Allows engineers to immediately spot accidental quadratic algorithms that would freeze browser tabs or servers.
lessons.what_learner_does: Analyzes multiple implementations of array search and sorting, plotting time complexity comparisons.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to evaluate time and space complexity of code intuitively.

lessons.lesson_title: Array & String Manipulation Patterns
lessons.what_is_taught: Two-pointer technique, sliding window basics, frequency counters, string palindrome checks, and anagrams.
lessons.why_it_matters: Arrays and strings form over 60% of entry-level technical coding interview screening questions.
lessons.what_learner_does: Solves 10 classic array and string interview problems (Two Sum, Valid Anagram, Reverse String, Max Subarray).
lessons.expected_outcome: Mastery of essential array and string interview patterns.

lessons.lesson_title: Hash Maps, Sets & Fast Lookup Data Structures
lessons.what_is_taught: Hash tables, Map and Set in JavaScript, O(1) average lookup times, caching, and deduplication patterns.
lessons.why_it_matters: Hash maps are the single most useful data structure in real software engineering for fast data retrieval.
lessons.what_learner_does: Solves 10 hash map challenges: group anagrams, first unique character, intersection of two arrays.
lessons.expected_outcome: Proficiency in leveraging hash maps for linear-time problem solving.

lessons.lesson_title: Stacks, Queues & Basic Recursion Patterns
lessons.what_is_taught: LIFO stack mechanics, FIFO queues, call stack recursion basics, base cases, and valid parentheses matching.
lessons.why_it_matters: Underpins browser history, undo/redo features, routing call stacks, and job processing queues.
lessons.what_learner_does: Solves classic stack problems (Valid Parentheses, Min Stack) and writes simple recursive tree/object traversals.
lessons.expected_outcome: Strong command of linear data structures and recursive thinking.

modules.hands_on_practice: Solve 30–40 practical coding challenges focusing on real software patterns rather than competitive trivia.
modules.assignment: Complete the Coding Interview Lab: submit verified solutions and Big-O explanations for 30 coding problems.
modules.business_application: Builds problem-solving speed and algorithmic intuition required to pass technical screening rounds at tech companies.
modules.expected_outcome: Strong algorithmic intuition and verified solutions to 30+ practical software engineering interview problems.

modules.module_title: Software Engineering Career Launch & Project Defense
modules.module_purpose: Prepare for technical hiring: engineer a recruiter-ready GitHub portfolio, resume, and defend code in viva juries.
what_you_will_learn: Master the core principles of Software Engineering Career Launch & Project Defense.
Implement production-grade practical code following modern industry best practices.
Systematically troubleshoot, test, and debug common real-world errors in this domain.

lessons.lesson_title: The Developer Resume & ATS Optimization
lessons.what_is_taught: Writing achievement-oriented bullet points (Action + Context + Metric), ATS keyword optimization, and tech stack summaries.
lessons.why_it_matters: Ensures your resume passes automated applicant tracking systems and catches engineering managers' attention.
lessons.what_learner_does: Drafts a technical developer resume highlighting projects, tech stack competencies, and live deployment links.
lessons.expected_outcome: ATS-optimized, clean software engineering resume.

lessons.lesson_title: GitHub Profile & Portfolio Showcase Engineering
lessons.what_is_taught: Structuring a compelling GitHub profile README, pinning best projects, writing great repo READMEs, and recording video demos.
lessons.why_it_matters: A clean GitHub profile with working live links provides instant verifiable proof-of-work to recruiters.
lessons.what_learner_does: Polishes GitHub profile and writes comprehensive READMEs with screenshots, architecture diagrams, and setup steps.
lessons.expected_outcome: Recruiter-ready GitHub profile showcasing 6 projects and 1 capstone.

lessons.lesson_title: Mastering the Technical Interview: JavaScript, React & SQL
lessons.what_is_taught: Common technical interview questions on closures, event loop, React rendering, SQL joins, REST design, and async code.
lessons.why_it_matters: Allows engineers to communicate complex technical concepts clearly and authoritatively during interviews.
lessons.what_learner_does: Participates in live 1-on-1 mock technical interview simulations with mentor feedback.
lessons.expected_outcome: Confidence explaining full-stack technical concepts clearly under pressure.

lessons.lesson_title: The Oral Project Defense: Defending Your Code
lessons.what_is_taught: Answering tough jury questions: 'Why PostgreSQL?', 'How does auth work?', 'What breaks at 10x scale?', 'How did you test this?'
lessons.why_it_matters: Proves you genuinely wrote, understand, and can defend every technical decision in your application.
lessons.what_learner_does: Presents flagship capstone project before faculty jury, defending architecture, schema, security, and trade-offs.
lessons.expected_outcome: Successful defense of capstone project and graduation qualification.

modules.hands_on_practice: Conduct a live project defense viva before faculty jury, explaining architectural decisions and code trade-offs.
modules.assignment: Submit finalized GitHub portfolio, polished developer resume, and complete the oral Technical Project Defense.
modules.business_application: Translates hard technical competence into credible professional positioning that secures developer interviews and offers.
modules.expected_outcome: Polished developer portfolio, verified resume, and demonstrated mastery defending technical decisions in interviews.
